sections.h2: Honey export value rose 83% in three years, to $177.55 million

chart.title: Export value grew from $96.77 million to $177.55 million
chart.source: PIB, National Beekeeping & Honey Mission backgrounder; APEDA/CRISIL.

sections.means: The export figures are the scheme's main success measure, and they have grown strongly.
sections.todo: Report domestic retail honey testing results alongside export results, since the scheme's metrics currently track exports only.

sections.h2: Registered colonies are about 1.6% of what the climate could support

chart.title: Only 1.93 million colonies are registered against an estimated 120 million
chart.source: APEDA (2023 registrations); research cited in the Indian Journal of Entomology.

sections.means: Registered colonies are a small share of the potential the post cites.
sections.todo: Set colony-growth targets for new beekeepers, tracked against the registered count.

sections.h2: The scheme leans toward Apis mellifera, which yielded nearly four times the honey

chart.title: Apis mellifera colonies made 25 kg of honey a year, Apis cerana 6.5 kg
chart.sub: Average honey per colony per year, kg.
chart.source: Punjab comparative study, as cited in the post.

sections.means: Apis mellifera also showed far lower colony absconding during the dearth period, which the study reports as 0% against 45%.
sections.todo: Weigh the honey yield gain against the temperament tradeoff when choosing bee species for subsidies.
